https://www.cp24.com/news/canada/2026/07.text: A fifth suspect has pleaded guilty in a human smuggling case that resulted in the death of a family, including two young kids under three years old, in the St. Lawrence River in March 2023. Stephanie Square, 53, a dual Canadian-American citizen from the Akwesasne Mohawk Territory, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit alien smuggling, four counts of alien smuggling for financial gain and four counts of alien smuggling resulting in death, the U.S. Department of Justice said Thursday. According to court documents, Square was a U.S. leader of a human smuggling organization that regularly trafficked migrants across the U.S.-Canada border in Akwesasne, the First Nations territory on the Quebec-Ontario border that also straddles the New York state border. During the week of March 27, 2023, a Canadian smuggler contacted Square to bring a Romanian couple and their two children across the St. Lawrence River into the United States. She also recruited co-conspirators to facilitate the operation, which went ahead despite dangerous weather conditions “so that she would be paid,” the documents stated. READ MORE: According to the DOJ, Square enlisted a driver, Dakota Montour, to drive the family on March 29, 2023, to the home of Timothy Oakes, whose home on Cornwall Island was a “notorious” staging area for human smuggling. After the family arrived, the family of four was transported in Oakes’ car to the tip of Cornwall Island, where Casey Oakes was waiting for them to bring them over the river. “While in transit, the boat capsized due to severe weather. As a result, the Romanian family and [Casey] Oakes died,” the DOJ said. A few days later, police searched the water and found the bodies of the four family members. Casey Oakes’ body was also found eight months later. After pleading guilty on Thursday, Square is set to be sentenced on Nov. 25. She faces a minimum penalty of five years in prison and a maximum of life in prison. Her co-conspirators, Dakota Montour, 32, Kawisiiostha Celecia Sharrow, 45, both of the Akwesasne Mohawk Indian reserve, New York, Janet Terrance, 46, of Hogansburg, N.Y., and Timothy Oakes, 35, from the Akwesasne Mohawk Indian reserve, already pleaded guilty on Jan. 23, 2025, Oct. 8, 2024, March 6, 2025, and May 11, 2026, respectively. Another co-conspirator, Rahsontanohstha Delormier, 31, pleaded guilty on June 26. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva called the deaths “a preventable and tragic loss of life.” “Human smuggling organizations show a reckless disregard for the safety and well-being of those they transport, often resulting in devastating consequences,” added Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone of U.S. Immigrations and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo. The DOJ said several partners assisted in the yearslong investigation, including the Canada Border Services Agency, the Akwesasne Mohawk Police Service, the Ontario Provincial Police, the Sûreté du Québec, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and the Cornwall Police Service, among others.

https://nineoclock.ro/romania-strengthen.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Oana Țoiu Meets Kazakhstan and Canada’s New Ambassadors to Strengthen Bilateral Ties Romania is seeking to deepen its bilateral relations with Kazakhstan and Canada, with economic cooperation, energy, security and strategic partnerships featuring prominently in recent diplomatic discussions in Bucharest. Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu received the designated ambassadors of Kazakhstan and Canada, H.E. Amangeldy Sainov and H.E. Kevin Rex, respectively, on August 10 and 13, on the occasion of the presentation of copies of their letters of credence, according to a press release issued by the Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE). Romania and Kazakhstan seek to expand economic and energy cooperation During her meeting with Kazakhstan’s designated ambassador, Amangeldy Sainov, Minister Oana Țoiu congratulated the new ambassador on his appointment and wished him success in carrying out his mandate. Romanian Foreign Minister H.E. Oana Țoiu & H.E. Amangeldy Sainov The Romanian minister highlighted the positive dynamics of bilateral relations and the constructive political and diplomatic dialogue between Bucharest and Astana. The meeting also reaffirmed the strong level of relations between the two countries, with discussions focusing on identifying concrete opportunities for future cooperation. An important milestone will be the planned organization this year in Astana of the 18th session of the Romania-Kazakhstan Intergovernmental Commission for Economic Cooperation. According to the MAE, Romania sees significant potential for developing economic ties with Kazakhstan by encouraging investment and diversifying bilateral trade. Energy remains a central pillar of the relationship, particularly in the context of regional energy security. The two sides also discussed the importance of continued cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including the economy, energy, connectivity and education. Romania and Canada deepen strategic partnership During her meeting with Canada’s designated ambassador, Kevin Rex, Oana Țoiu underlined the excellent state of Romanian-Canadian relations and the convergence of views between the two countries on key international issues. Romanian Foreign Minister H.E. Oana Țoiu & H.E. Kevin Rex The discussions covered a broad range of topics, including strengthening NATO effectiveness, energy security and continued support for Ukraine, including efforts related to the return of Ukrainian children and support for multilateral formats. The Romanian foreign minister also referred to the substantial bilateral dialogue conducted this year, including the meeting between Romanian President Nicușor Dan and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on the sidelines of the NATO Summit in Ankara, as well as the visit to Romania by the Canadian foreign minister on July 6. The meeting provided an opportunity to review achievements and priorities under the Enhanced Partnership between Romania and Canada. Security cooperation remains an important component of the partnership. Canada is involved in MCM Black Sea and in nuclear projects at Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant. The discussions also highlighted progress in the planned refurbishment of Unit 1 and the construction of Units 3 and 4 at the Cernavodă nuclear facility. Another area of cooperation concerns the planned creation of a Bank for Defence, Security and Resilience, with a regional office in Romania. Focus on trade, defence industry and transatlantic supply chains Economic and commercial cooperation was also highlighted as an area with significant potential for further development. Oana Țoiu emphasized the importance of developing joint projects and partnerships and integrating Romanian and Canadian companies into transatlantic supply chains, including those linked to the defence industry. The two countries’ shared experience and broadly aligned values and views on international developments provide a strong foundation for expanding economic cooperation, according to the Romanian Foreign Ministry. The partnership also has an important human dimension, reflected in cultural and educational exchanges. These links contribute to the continuity of the framework established through the Enhanced Partnership Declaration and help maintain long-standing ties between the citizens of Romania and Canada. Romania reaffirms commitment to stronger bilateral partnerships The meetings with the designated ambassadors of Kazakhstan and Canada provided an opportunity for Romania to reaffirm its commitment to deepening bilateral relations and developing concrete forms of cooperation for the benefit of citizens in all three countries. At the conclusion of the meetings, Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu wished both designated ambassadors success in carrying out their mandates and assured them of the full support of the Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in their diplomatic activities. Source: Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE), press release dated August 13, 2026.
